-- A sent or part-paid invoice that will never be paid can be written off as bad debt. It stays on
-- record but is no longer owed.
ALTER TABLE invoice DROP CONSTRAINT invoice_status_valid;
ALTER TABLE invoice ADD CONSTRAINT invoice_status_valid
    CHECK (status IN ('DRAFT', 'SENT', 'PARTIAL', 'PAID', 'VOID', 'WRITTEN_OFF'));
-- Part of a sent or part-paid invoice can be written off as bad debt. The written-off part is no longer
-- owed; the rest still is. Existing invoices have nothing written off.
ALTER TABLE invoice ADD COLUMN write_off_amount DECIMAL(12, 2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0;
ALTER TABLE invoice ADD CONSTRAINT invoice_write_off_amount_not_negative CHECK (write_off_amount >= 0);

content.text:
A partial write-off now shows as its own line in the invoice breakdown with the test IDs the spec expects, and `bin/e2e` passes.

**One front-end change, no migration or server work.** The database (`write_off_amount`, added in V81), the server and the API response already carried the written-off amount. The invoice page also already had a "Written off as bad debt" line, shown whenever the amount is above zero, with the IDs `invoice-write-off-row` and `invoice-write-off-amount`. The only thing missing was the two IDs the test looks for.

**How I added them:** an element can only hold one `data-testid`, and the existing IDs can't be renamed. So in `src/main/frontend/src/app/features/invoices/invoice-detail.ts` I nested two new spans inside the existing amount cell:
- `breakdown-writeoff-row` wraps `breakdown-writeoff-amount`, which shows the amount (e.g. `$40.00`).
- This copies how the discount lines already do it with `breakdown-discount-row-{id}`.

One downside: `breakdown-writeoff-row` sits on a span inside the amount cell, not on the table row, because the row already has its own ID.

**Gap: writing off a whole invoice doesn't produce this line.** The full write-off only changes the invoice's status to "written off" and doesn't store an amount, so the line stays hidden. Partial write-offs and seeded write-off amounts do show. If "any write-off" should include the full kind, the server would need to save the written-off balance as well. I left that alone because it's beyond what the test checks.
